writeup: TIC 307453359 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.7401 days. The TESS mission detected a primary eclipse showing a 7.11% dimming in the star's light, with a strong automated detection signal-to-noise ratio of 107.2. Pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirmed the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 31.5, though the centroid offset measured 1.4 arcsec from the target. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. While the machine-learning screening score of 0.34 indicates moderate confidence from the automated pipeline, this object merits further investigation to determine whether it represents a genuine eclipsing binary system.
